# sing-box-vps Agent Index

Project: sing-box-vps
Purpose: one-script install and management tool for deploying sing-box on Linux VPS hosts.
Primary language: Bash.
Runtime source of truth: install.sh.
Remote verification: Docker-based, auto-builds sing-box-vps-verify image.

Canonical documents:
- AGENTS.md: repository rules, validation requirements, SSH alias conventions, version rules.
- README.md: user-facing install, features, versions, runtime paths.
- docs/agents/sing-box-vps-agent-runbook.md: AI agent operations manual for repository maintenance, test VPS validation, production plans, install, upgrade, troubleshooting, and rollback.
- docs/agents/sing-box-1.13-to-1.14-upgrade-test.md: Hermes single-host fixed-version rehearsal with evidence and stop gates.
- skills/sing-box-vps-operator/SKILL.md: AgentSkills-style triggerable skill for Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, and similar agents.
- dev/verification/run.sh: local and remote verification entrypoint.
- dev/verification/docker/Dockerfile: Docker verification image definition.

Key runtime paths:
- /root/sing-box-vps/
- /root/sing-box-vps/config.json
- /root/sing-box-vps/protocols/
- /root/sing-box-vps-backups/ (root-only Agent upgrade backups; sensitive)
- /usr/local/bin/sbv
- systemd service: sing-box

Agent CLI:

- Standalone HTTP uses protocol ID http, menu preset 6, and the shared schema-2 instance lifecycle (create/replace/delete/default/recover, never migrate). Typed records additionally require tls: {enabled:false} or {enabled:true,server_name,certificate_path,key_path}. HTTP CONNECT client export is TCP-only; TLS export embeds public certificate trust, never the server key. TLS URI material is unavailable with http_tls_uri_unrepresentable: use export-client JSON. No HTTP SubMan sync. Existing Mixed/SOCKS formats are unchanged.

- Mixed/SOCKS share URI userinfo is percent-encoded byte-for-byte. For Mixed credentials that HTTP Basic cannot represent (colon in username or ASCII control characters), links omits HTTP and returns mixed_http_auth_unrepresentable without changing credentials; SOCKS5 remains available. socks5_uri_transport_options_omitted warns that the URI does not carry UoT v2 options: use export-client JSON for full configuration. Encoding is not encryption.
- sbv agent capabilities --json: machine-readable capability matrix; read-only, no secrets.
- sbv agent upgrade-check --json 1.14.0: read-only eligibility preflight that does not reconcile or migrate state; inspect ready, blockers, config hash/schema, legacy fields, and warnings. It does not download the target binary.
- sbv agent upgrade --json 1.14.0 --yes: guarded binary upgrade; mutating and service-impacting, with automatic backup under /root/sing-box-vps-backups/, a manifest covering every regular runtime file plus control files, and an atomic transaction-result.json audit record.
- sbv agent status --json: service/version/paths/protocols plus network stacks, BBR, REALITY/QoS counts, and integration presence.
- sbv agent nodes --json: log-safe summaries for every protocol and every REALITY/Mixed/SOCKS instance, including instance revision without credentials.
- sbv agent links --json: full per-protocol and per-REALITY/Mixed/SOCKS-instance connection material; treat output as sensitive.
- sbv agent export-client --json: generate and validate /root/sing-box-vps/client/sing-box-client.json without changing the running server config.
- sbv agent check --json: run sing-box check against the server config and return structured stdout/stderr/status.
- sbv agent doctor --json: read-only diagnostics with service, paths, protocols, and embedded config check.
- sbv agent warp --json: read-only Warp/account/routing summary.
- sbv agent service restart --json --yes: guarded restart after config validation; production use requires approval.
- sbv agent subman-sync --json: non-interactive SubMan node push; treat as sensitive and require configured /root/sing-box-vps/subman.env.

Capability safety labels:
- read-only: status, capabilities, upgrade-check, check, doctor, nodes, warp.
- mutating: upgrade, service restart, export-client, subman-sync.
- sensitive: links, export-client, subman-sync; these may expose usable credentials or external node data.
- instance <operation> socks: mutating, service-impacting and revision/CAS guarded; lifecycle passed the final local/Docker/core verification gate. This does not mean the full protocol goal is complete.
- interactive-only: fresh install, protocol changes, REALITY instance/QoS changes, Warp changes, BBR/system changes, media checks, takeover/repair, uninstall.

Capability domains to preserve in documentation and tests:
- protocols: VLESS REALITY, Mixed HTTP/SOCKS, standalone SOCKS, Hysteria2, AnyTLS, coexistence.
- REALITY: multi-instance, per-instance port/ShortID/name/outbound, upload/download QoS.
- TLS: ACME HTTP-01, Cloudflare DNS-01, manual certificates, Hysteria2 Ed25519 client warning.
- routing/system: Warp all/selective routing, custom and local/remote rule sets, IPv4/IPv6/dual stack, DNS/outbound strategy, BBR.
- operations: service lifecycle/logs, node/link/QR output, client export, SubMan, takeover/repair, core/script upgrade, core/script uninstall.

SSH aliases:
- sing-box-test: test VPS for validation.
- sing-box-prod: production VPS. Production-changing commands require a plan and explicit approval first.

Important requirements:
- Run sing-box check after modifying or generating sing-box server or client configs.
- Back up existing runtime configuration before changing production state.
- Docker-based remote verification: see dev/verification/run.sh and dev/verification/docker/Dockerfile.
- Run bash dev/verification/run.sh after changes to install.sh, uninstall.sh, configs/, utils/, or dev/verification/.
- Do not reveal secrets, private keys, passwords, tokens, full node links, or QR payloads unless explicitly requested and safe.
- Treat sbv agent links --json, export-client --json, and subman-sync --json as sensitive connection-material commands.
- Upgrade backups contain the full runtime state and must never be copied into shared logs or artifacts.
- Agent JSON uses schema_version "1.0" with the legacy schema "1" retained. For upgrades that change the installed version, require transaction.result_persisted=true and inspect transaction.result_path, status, manifest hash, and rollback result. If the target version is already installed, accept only changed=false with transaction.status=not_attempted and transaction.reason=already_installed; no backup or transaction result file is created.
- Do not run production install, upgrade, restart, stop, uninstall, purge, firewall mutation, or config overwrite without an approved production operation plan.

Common task routing:
- Fresh install on new VPS: read README.md and docs/agents/sing-box-vps-agent-runbook.md.
- Upgrade existing VPS: read docs/agents/sing-box-vps-agent-runbook.md, then prepare a production operation plan for sing-box-prod.
- Hermes 1.13 to 1.14 rehearsal: first update sbv, then read docs/agents/sing-box-1.13-to-1.14-upgrade-test.md and run its preflight/evidence gates before any core mutation.
- Test remote verification: read dev/verification/run.sh, dev/verification/common.sh, and AGENTS.md.
- Production troubleshooting: use read-only checks first, then prepare a production operation plan for changes.
- AI agent node info retrieval: prefer sbv agent nodes --json for summaries and sbv agent links --json only in trusted contexts.
- VLESS REALITY multi-instance or rate-limit work: use script-managed state under /root/sing-box-vps/protocols/vless-reality.d/ and /root/sing-box-vps/reality-qos.filters; do not hand-edit generated config.json.
- REALITY takeover retains existing instance IDs, names, QoS and the default instance by matching saved inbound tags. Connection parameters follow the live config; an old public key is retained only when its private key matches. Ambiguous saved tags stop reconstruction before state replacement.
- Instance reads use the shared protocol/instance adapter. Legacy singleton state is exposed internally as main; REALITY keeps its existing multi-instance IDs, while Mixed and standalone SOCKS use active schema-2 markers with JSON stores whose `schema_version` is 1, and expose instance revisions. Agent reads and client rendering do not migrate legacy state or create credentials.
- The typed stores under protocols/instances/ now have Mixed and standalone SOCKS handlers. Mixed supports `sbv agent instance create|replace|delete|default|migrate|recover mixed --json --yes --expected-revision N`; standalone SOCKS supports the same commands except `migrate`, which returns invalid arguments because it has no legacy `.env` migration path. Existing live SOCKS configuration uses takeover. Create/replace require a complete private `--file` record, delete/default require `--id`, and recover requires the original journal revision. SOCKS records describe only SOCKS inbound listen/authentication, never HTTP or TLS. The standalone SOCKS lifecycle and runtime/export paths passed the final verification gate; do not infer complete support for TLS, HTTP, SubMan, public native UDP, or the full protocol goal from registry presence. See `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-06-unified-protocol-management.md` for the evidence boundary.
- Server candidates and typed stores reject overlapping managed fixed listeners before publication. Firewall cleanup compares the previous config backup with remaining listeners, retaining referenced transport/port rules. Missing or unmodelled inventories block cleanup; backend failure is nonzero and may leave partial external changes. This is reference protection, not proof of ownership of existing firewall rules or a complete system-resource rollback.
- Firewall opening reads the complete committed listener plan and opens only registered listening transports. Full protocol removal requires a successful stop and confirmed inactive service before clearing config/index and rules. Post-publication opening failure reports config_committed, firewall_may_be_partial and service_restart_not_attempted; inspect the service manually rather than assuming rollback.
- Client export: use sbv agent export-client --json and remember it writes /root/sing-box-vps/client/sing-box-client.json with backup/validation. Mixed and standalone SOCKS export as SOCKS5 with UoT v2; authentication is preserved, never generated or silently disabled. Missing/invalid port or auth state blocks the whole export without replacing the existing file/backup. The plaintext transport warning means the proxy transport has no TLS, including exposed credentials; use a trusted network or protected tunnel. UoT is not encryption. Standalone SOCKS has no HTTP/TLS surface or SubMan sync, and its export/runtime paths passed the final gate; public native UDP and the full protocol goal remain unproven.
- SubMan sync: use sbv agent subman-sync --json only when SubMan config exists and the target context is trusted.
- Repository maintenance: read AGENTS.md, affected scripts, and run verification as required.
- sing-box config syntax or migration: use Context7 first; fall back to official sing-box docs or repository only when needed.

Search keywords:
install, upgrade, production, Docker verification, rollback, recovery, sbv agent, node info, connection links, client export, SubMan sync, sing-box check, sing-box-prod, dev/verification/run.sh, config.json, protocols, Warp, VLESS REALITY, REALITY multi-instance, rate limits, QoS, Hysteria2, AnyTLS, Mixed proxy, standalone SOCKS, systemctl sing-box.

Protocol registry:
- Client export candidates pass reference validation and the target core check before publication. `client_config_validation_failed` preserves the previous export and backup; diagnostics remain on stderr.
- `sbv agent capabilities --json` includes additive `protocol_registry` metadata from install.sh. Legacy `protocols` keys and envelope remain compatible.
- Separate family/preset/role/state_id/agent_id; legacy `vless` still resolves to the REALITY preset, Hysteria2 state ID remains `hy2`, and standalone SOCKS is the fifth registry preset with menu order 5 and state/Agent ID `socks`.
- `implemented` describes the project adapter; `available=null` and `validated.status=not_assessed` do not certify the current environment or connection. Perform instance preflight/check and inspect real probe artifacts.
- Unknown state IDs/schema versions and invalid builder fragments block reconstruction without removing those entries. Use a compatible script or restore a reviewed backup; do not delete unknown state to bypass the guard.
- Live inbound discovery is all-or-nothing. Unknown types, non-REALITY VLESS, duplicate single-instance protocols, or duplicate explicit tags make the instance incomplete and block reconciliation, takeover, regeneration, and partial Agent status/node/link output. The three Agent commands return `live_inbound_inventory_untrusted` without exposing a partial list. They also require an exact live-config/index set match and a complete base-state inventory, returning `protocol_index_untrusted` or `protocol_state_untrusted`; `nodes`/`links` additionally reject incomplete REALITY instance enumeration and discard rendered nodes if any later load or state restoration fails. This is an inbound-inventory guard, not proof that custom fields, outbounds, endpoints, or routes are losslessly managed.
- Full-scope progress: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-06-unified-protocol-management.md; upstream evidence: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-protocol-coverage.md.
